chapters.title: Chapter 0: Purpose and Learning Outcomes
chapters.content:
Purpose

A retail payment is complete only after authorization, capture, settlement, and reconciliation succeed under compliance controls.

Payment failure is one of the fastest paths to direct revenue loss.

Learning Outcomes

  • Explain authorization, capture, settlement, and reconciliation
  • Identify common payment failures and incident signals
  • Understand PCI scope and card-data protection boundaries
  • Classify payment incidents by severity
  • Define fraud indicators and response workflows
  • Apply AI safely in payment operations

checkpoint.answer: Funds must be captured, settled, and reconciled, not just authorized.

chapters.title: Chapter 1: Payment Ecosystem Fundamentals
chapters.content:
Customer -> POS -> Gateway -> Card Network -> Issuer Bank -> Response -> POS

Core participants: customer, merchant, payment gateway, card network, issuer bank, and acquirer bank.

A sale on receipt is not cash in account until settlement completes.

checkpoint.answer: Because incident ownership and escalation depend on where failure occurs in the payment chain.

chapters.title: Chapter 2: Authorization
chapters.content:
Authorization asks: is this transaction allowed right now?

Issuer Validation

  • Card status and validity
  • Available balance/credit
  • Fraud and risk checks
  • Account restrictions

Responses

  • Approved
  • Declined
  • Timeout

Timeout spikes often increase customer retries and duplicate-attempt risk.

checkpoint.answer: No, authorization only reserves/permits payment; capture and settlement must still occur.

chapters.title: Chapter 3: Capture
chapters.content:
Capture submits the approved amount for transfer processing.

Authorization -> Capture Request -> Clearing/Settlement Pipeline

Capture Models

  • Immediate capture: common in store checkout
  • Delayed capture: common in e-commerce/travel/hospitality

Capture gaps can create approved transactions without downstream funds.

checkpoint.prompt: What is the key distinction of capture?
checkpoint.answer: Capture initiates fund transfer after authorization.

chapters.title: Chapter 4: Settlement
chapters.content:
Customer Bank -> Card Network -> Acquirer -> Retailer Account

Settlement is typically batch-based and may complete after checkout day.

Risks

  • Missing settlement after successful sale
  • Duplicate settlement submission
  • Delayed batch processing

Settlement quality directly affects cashflow predictability and finance controls.

checkpoint.prompt: Why can sales and cash disagree temporarily?
checkpoint.answer: Because settlement and bank posting can lag checkout completion.

chapters.title: Chapter 5: Payment Reconciliation
chapters.content:
Reconciliation verifies consistency across POS, gateway, settlement files, bank statements, and ERP.

Collect Data -> Compare Records -> Find Variance -> Root Cause -> Correct

Common Variances

  • Missing capture
  • Duplicate transaction
  • Settlement failure
  • Offline upload delay
  • Batch processing mismatch

checkpoint.answer: Collect and align records from all source systems before root-cause analysis.

chapters.title: Chapter 6: Payment Failure Taxonomy
chapters.content:
CategorySymptomsLikely Impact
Authorization failuresDecline spike, tender unavailableImmediate conversion drop
TimeoutsLong waits, retry stormsAbandonment and duplicates
Duplicate chargesMultiple auth/capture recordsChargebacks and trust loss
Settlement failureCompleted sales, missing depositsCashflow and accounting risk
Gift card issuesWrong balances, rejectsStore escalations and delay

checkpoint.answer: Authorization failures, timeouts, and duplicate charge incidents.

chapters.title: Chapter 7: PCI Compliance Fundamentals
chapters.content:
PCI DSS defines controls for payment card data protection.

Sensitive Data

  • PAN (card number)
  • CVV
  • Track data
  • PIN-related data

PCI Scope

POS, PIN pads, payment applications, and payment network touchpoints are typically in scope.

Control Objectives

  • Protect and encrypt cardholder data
  • Restrict access
  • Maintain audit trails
  • Monitor security events

checkpoint.prompt: Why does PCI scope clarity matter?
checkpoint.answer: It determines where strict controls, auditability, and security obligations are mandatory.

chapters.title: Chapter 8: Fraud in Retail Payments
chapters.content:
Fraud Types

  • Stolen card usage
  • Friendly fraud disputes
  • Gift card fraud
  • Refund fraud
  • Employee fraud

Indicators

  • High-value velocity spikes
  • High decline then approval patterns
  • Excessive refund concentration by operator
  • Tender anomalies by store/time window

Fraud controls should reduce false positives while preserving checkout flow.

checkpoint.prompt: What is a common card-testing indicator?
checkpoint.answer: Large decline volumes followed by intermittent approvals.

chapters.title: Chapter 9: Severity Classification for Payment Incidents
chapters.content:
SeverityExampleResponse
SEV1Chain-wide payment outageWar room + executive escalation
SEV2Regional outage or major tender failureRapid escalation + command coordination
SEV3Store-local or intermittent issueStandard incident process
SEV4Minor config/terminal defectPlanned remediation

checkpoint.answer: Revenue-at-risk multiplied by scope and customer impact.

chapters.title: Chapter 10: Incident Response Playbooks
chapters.content:
Gateway Outage Playbook

  • Detect: authorization failures and timeout spike
  • Validate: gateway health, network path, error classes
  • Mitigate: failover route, backup tender messaging
  • Communicate: store guidance and status cadence

Duplicate Charge Playbook

  • Investigate retries and idempotency
  • Reverse duplicate charges
  • Issue customer communication
  • Fix retry/root-cause logic

checkpoint.answer: Idempotency controls and corrected retry behavior with clear timeout handling.

chapters.title: Chapter 11: Payment KPIs
chapters.content:
Authorization Rate = Approved / Authorization Attempts
Settlement Success Rate = Settled / Captured
  • Chargeback rate: lower is better
  • Payment latency: lower improves checkout conversion
  • Tender mix: informs strategy and risk concentration

High latency can be as damaging as outright decline spikes in peak hours.

checkpoint.prompt: Which KPI exposes checkout friction quickly?
checkpoint.answer: Payment latency and authorization success trend together expose friction early.

chapters.title: Chapter 12: AI in Payments and Risk
chapters.content:
AI Opportunities

  • Payment health agent for outage precursors
  • Fraud signal agent for suspicious behavior patterns
  • Reconciliation agent for variance detection
  • RCA draft agent for incident evidence synthesis

Safety Boundary

AI should recommend and prioritize; human owners approve high-risk actions affecting money movement or compliance obligations.

checkpoint.prompt: Best first AI use case in payments?
checkpoint.answer: Payment health monitoring with anomaly detection and clear human escalation paths.
